gravityContext.female: Dizziness when standing can occur after returning to gravity following a period in microgravity. Report symptoms to the onboard team and follow your individual readaptation protocol. NASA describes greater susceptibility to orthostatic intolerance among women in the cited studies; this does not determine individual risk or change this app's ranges.
gravityContext.other: Dizziness when standing can occur after returning to gravity following a period in microgravity. Report symptoms to the onboard team and follow your individual readaptation protocol. Responses vary between people; this note does not estimate individual risk or change this app's ranges.

goals.title: Weekly goals
goals.intro: In how many of the last {{window}} days, counting today, each indicator stayed in the green range. The goal is {{target}} days, leaving room for days outside the routine. Demo goal, not a prescription: each crew member's plan comes from the medical team.

profile.intro: Sentinela works for any spacecraft. The profile sets the mission type, length, and phases; today's phase sets the environment.

alarms.title: Alarm volume
alarms.intro: Yellow plays one short tone. Red repeats the sound until someone silences or confirms it. Every sound also appears as a fixed notice at the top of the screen.
alarms.note: Silence stops the sound, but the notice only goes away when someone confirms it. On phones, the notice also vibrates when the device allows it (iPhone does not). The voice says only the alert level, with no health details, because everyone in the cabin can hear it.

crewStatus.title: Crew
crewStatus.intro: Here you can only see whether each crewmate completed today's check-in and whether there is a red alert. The commander cannot see health data. If there is a red alert, call the onboard medical officer.
crewStatus.empty: No other crew members to show.
crewStatus.accessLog: Only information that has reached the onboard hub is counted. This view is recorded in each crewmate's access log.

sync.title: Synchronization
sync.intro: Everything happens automatically. The check-in goes from the device to the onboard hub over the ship's network, and the hub sends one packet per day to the medical team on Earth whenever there is a connection. Without a connection, packets wait and leave when it returns. Alerts never wait for Earth; immediate decisions are made onboard.
sync.failed: The last synchronization failed ({{error}}). It will retry automatically every 5 seconds.
sync.hubIntro: Receives records from all devices on the ship.
sync.delay: One-way delay in the current environment ({{environment}}): {{delay}}. Red alerts are prioritized.
sync.offline: No connection. Packets wait at the hub and are sent automatically when the connection returns.
sync.noServer: · No Earth server configured. Packets only appear to arrive here for the demo.
sync.unreachable: The Earth server did not respond. Packets wait at the hub and sending is retried automatically.
sync.recentPackets: Most recent packets. Queued packets appear first, in sending order.

ground.notice: Data arrives in packets when a communication window is available, with a one-way delay of {{delay}} ({{environment}}). Information here may have changed onboard. Immediate decisions are always made onboard.

stored.title: What stays in this browser
stored.text: Fictional profile (name, role, sex, and mission start), tracked indicators, medication plan, check-in values and symptoms, medical officer notes, messages, access log, deletion requests, and preferences. Check-in values, notes, and message text are encrypted. Alerts, correlations, and baseline are calculated from the records.

purpose.title: Purpose
purpose.text: To demonstrate indicator monitoring, comparison with ranges and personal patterns, and the organization of information for a discussion with the medical officer. Use fictional information only; this prototype does not provide health care.

access.title: Who can see it
access.text: Each person signs in with their own profile and PIN. In the app, crew members see only their own data; the onboard medical officer sees everyone's; the commander sees only whether each crewmate checked in and whether there is a red alert; the medical team on Earth receives one encrypted packet per crew member each day. Each view of your data is recorded in Your data. Your data is encrypted with a key that belongs to you and can be opened with your PIN and the medical officer's PIN; another crewmate's PIN cannot open it. Prototype limitations: someone who copies the database may discover the short PIN, and the ground physician's key is in this same browser because everything runs on one device. Exporting creates a file under your control; opening external sources accesses those websites.

retention.title: How long data is kept
retention.text: Health data is a mission record and stays on the device until browser storage is cleared or the demo is recreated; sent packets are also held by the team on Earth. The browser may remove its storage. Downloaded JSON files are separate copies and must be deleted where they were saved.

legal.title: Legal basis and prototype limitations
legal.text: For a real service, Brazil's LGPD provides for health protection under article 11, II, f, exclusively in procedures carried out by health professionals, health services, or a health authority. This basis does not automatically apply to this demo. Before using real data, the responsible organization must define the legal basis and required safeguards. Continuing here records only that you read this notice, not generic consent to process health data.

rights.title: Your rights
rights.text: Article 18 of the LGPD provides rights such as access, correction, and, where legally applicable, deletion. The Your data screen offers a JSON copy and a way to register a deletion request for the team to review: crew members cannot delete their own health history. This app does not promise remote care or full LGPD compliance.

medication.title: Medication and protection limits
medication.text: The medication plan contains names and scheduled times. If linked to a real person, it is sensitive health data. In this prototype, the plan stays in the profile without encryption, as do the profile data and the indicator list. Anyone with access to the browser storage can read them without a PIN. Daily marks for medication taken, stress, workload, and exercise times are encrypted with the other check-in values. Use only fictional data.

missionContext.title: Calculated mission context
missionContext.text: The mission profile and environment stay in the device's shared preferences, without encryption. The bone estimate and the sum of recorded radiation doses are calculated on screen, without creating a new measurement. The JSON copy includes the recorded daily doses, but not these calculations or the shared mission preferences. The demo data is simulated.

reactionAndSource.title: Reaction test and declared source
reactionAndSource.text: The check-in can store the average reaction time in milliseconds, short or full mode, completion, duration, number of valid responses, and anticipations. This data and the declared source of values are encrypted with the check-in and appear readable in the JSON copy. We do not store each tap, recordings, or device identification. Selecting wearable sensor or dosimeter only states where you copied the number from; the app does not read devices. Weekly goals and readaptation notices are calculated on screen, without diagnosis.

yourData.title: Your data
yourData.intro: The actions below apply only to your data, for the profile you used to sign in.
yourData.encryption: Check-in values, notes, and message text are encrypted with one key per crew member, opened by your PIN and by the medical officer's. The profile and the medication plan are not encrypted. Prototype limit: the short PIN can be guessed by anyone who copies the database.
yourData.copyIncludes: The copy includes the profile and the medication plan, the check-ins (including medication taken, stress, workload, exercise, reaction test result and details, and declared source, when recorded), the medical officer's notes, messages, the access log, and the deletion request. It does not include other crew members' data. The downloaded JSON file is readable, not encrypted; store it carefully. It is a copy for reference, without import or regulated portability.
yourData.exportDone: JSON file prepared for download. It contains only this profile's data.
yourData.requestDone: Request recorded. Nothing was deleted: the health history belongs to the mission, and the request is for the team to review.
yourData.noDelete: Crew members cannot delete their own health history: it is a mission record. The deletion request is recorded for the team to review under LGPD article 18; nothing is deleted immediately.
yourData.readError: Could not read the deletion request.
yourData.operationError: Could not complete the operation in local storage. Try again.
yourData.accessIntro: In the app, the onboard medical officer sees your values and alerts, the medical team on Earth sees daily packets, and the commander sees only whether you checked in and whether there is a red alert. Each view is recorded here.
yourData.nobody: No one other than you has opened your data.

medicalContact.title: Message to the medical officer
medicalContact.intro: If you cannot speak, write a message to show the onboard medical officer.
medicalContact.urgent: This app does not send messages or provide care. In an urgent situation, contact the onboard team using the available method. Do not wait for a response on this screen.
medicalContact.prompt: What would you like to communicate? Use only a fictional example.
medicalContact.help: You can describe what you felt and when it started. {{count}}/{{max}} characters. There is no sending, read receipt, or response-time estimate.
medicalContact.saved: Message saved only on this device. It was not sent to the medical officer. Show them this screen.
medicalContact.saveError: Could not save. Check the text and try again.
medicalContact.none: No messages saved for this profile.
medicalContact.export: Export data or record a deletion request in Your data →

disclaimer.details: Decision support, no diagnosis. Simulated crew data and demo ranges. CosmoTI team · NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026.

boneLoss.estimate: Estimate, not a measurement: for {{days}} in microgravity, the illustrative calculation is around {{min}}% to {{max}}%. It multiplies by time an average published by NASA for weight-bearing bones ({{rateMin}}% to {{rateMax}}% per month, in missions of {{monthsMin}} to {{monthsMax}} months). It does not measure or predict your bone loss; exercise, diet, and individual differences affect the result.
boneLoss.beyondStudied: After {{months}} months, do not assume the loss continues at the same rate; linear extrapolation has not been validated.
boneLoss.partial_one: {{count}} day was in partial gravity (Moon or Mars), where the loss rate is unknown; that day is not counted.
boneLoss.partial_other: {{count}} days were in partial gravity (Moon or Mars), where the loss rate is unknown; those days are not counted.
boneLoss.shortPeriod: This period is shorter than the {{monthsMin}} to {{monthsMax}} months cited in the source: extrapolating the average to a short mission has not been validated.

radiation.total: Estimate, not a measurement: {{dose}} accumulated in this mission, {{percent}}% of the NASA career limit of {{limit}} mSv{{priorNote}} (adding up {{days}} with an entered value). The demo data is simulated; the app is not connected to a dosimeter.
radiation.missing_one: {{count}} day without a valid reading is not in the sum. The recorded total is incomplete; the exposure on that day cannot be determined.
radiation.missing_other: {{count}} days without a valid reading are not in the sum. The recorded total is incomplete; the exposure on those days cannot be determined.
radiation.notLimit: This is context and an estimate, not an official limit: NASA's institutional calculation uses effective dose and specialized clinical evaluation.
